records.title: First Aid and Paramedic Services
records.description: Liverpool Experience Campus (LEX) is looking for suitably qualified suppliers of event first aid and paramedic services for events that are held on Campus across the M&S Bank Arena, the Auditorium, Conference Centre and Exhibition Centre Liverpool. The aim for this service is to ensure that there is an appropriate level of medical, first aid and ambulance provision at an event to keep attendees safe and minimise the impact on local NHS services. The supplier will be required to: • Undertake a medical, ambulance and first aid assessment • Produce a medical staffing plan prior to each event to ensure that staff are deployed appropriately • Provide medical provision for the full duration of each event, including build up and derig Further information can be found within the tender documentation, which is available via Delta eSourcing Portal. LEX is looking to award an initial 2-year contract with the option to extend for a further 2-year period. Extension will be at the sole discretion of LEX. The contract has been valued at approximately £100,000 per year and therefore is valued at £400,000 for the entire contract including optional extensions. The contract start date will be approximately Thursday 1st April 2027. However, the exact start date will need to be flexible depending on LEX event bookings scheduled during this Easter holiday time. For example, if there is an event that covers the Easter school holidays and ends on Sunday 4th April 2027, then this contract will commence on Monday 5th April 2027. The exact start date will be confirmed to the successful tenderer either on contract award or event confirmation – whichever is sooner. Tenderers are invited to attend an individual tenderer’s tour of the Liverpool Experience Campus operations to view the site and operational areas that are currently used for first aid and paramedic services to assist in tender preparation. These site visits will be available at the sole discretion of LEX between the dates of Tuesday 3rd and Friday 13th November 2026 and will be allocated on a first come, first served basis. Tenderers are required to contact the procurement team as soon as possible via the Delta eSourcing Portal messaging facility to arrange this. Any requests received after Friday 13th November 2026 may not be considered by LEX due to operational and security constraints. For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Liverpool:-Paramedical-services./3F848ZF9QJ To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/3F848ZF9QJ

records.title: Welfare Advice Services and Advice Network Support & Training Services
records.authority: City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council
records.description: The City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council is procuring Welfare Advice Services and Advice Network Support and Training Services to support residents experiencing financial hardship, poverty and barriers to accessing support across Bradford District. The service is funded through the Crisis and Resilience Fund and aims to improve financial wellbeing, resilience and access to welfare support. The procurement comprises two lots. Lot 1 – Welfare Advice Services will provide free, independent, impartial and confidential welfare advice, casework and representation for Bradford District residents. The service will support residents with welfare benefits, debt, housing, employment, health-related welfare issues, fuel poverty, consumer matters and immigration advice within the provider's authorised competence. The Lead Provider will deliver services directly and coordinate a network of subcontracted locality-based organisations to ensure access across all five Bradford localities. The service will operate on a "no wrong front door" basis, ensuring residents receive timely support, active referrals and appropriate advocacy where required. Lot 2 – Advice Network Support and Training Services will support workforce development, quality improvement, collaboration and network coordination across the Bradford District Resilience and Advice Network. The Provider will facilitate partnership working, deliver a district-wide training programme, support consistent reporting and quality standards, strengthen safeguarding awareness and develop pathways into accredited welfare advice roles. The services will contribute to the Council's Anti-Poverty Strategy, support prevention of homelessness, improve financial resilience, increase benefit uptake, strengthen partnership working and improve outcomes for vulnerable residents across the district. The initial contract term is two years with options to extend for up to two further periods of 24 months.

The scope of works shall include, but not be limited to: • Assessment of the existing MRF operation and site constraints. • Design of a new MRF layout and processing line. • Removal and disposal, or relocation where applicable, of existing MRF equipment. • Supply of all new equipment required for the proposed solution. • Integration of both existing and new equipment into the redesigned processing line. • Installation, commissioning, performance testing, and handover of the complete system. • Provision of operator training and relevant documentation. • Provision of warranties for all new equipment supplied under the Contract. • Provision of ongoing maintenance and support services, including details of response times and planned preventative maintenance arrangements. The Tenderer shall demonstrate that the proposed solution represents best value for money and is capable of delivering a safe, efficient, reliable, and future-ready recycling operation throughout the contract term. records.title: Direct Payment Support Service
records.description: Newcastle City Council is seeking to appoint an organisation to provide a Direct Payment Support Service to adults, children and carers who use, or are considering using, direct payments to purchase or arrange services. Direct payments can be used to purchase care and support service to meet the care and support needs of the person and carer. Direct payments do involve additional complexity and responsibility for the service user and therefore many need some support and/or advice. The Direct Payment Support Service Newcastle City Council are procuring will: -Information and Advice Explain the benefits and responsibilities of direct payments to Service Users Assist with budgeting and expenditure decisions Provide information about the range of services that provide payroll, insurance and pensions and signpost direct payment users. -Employment Support Provide advice on becoming an employer Support payroll, tax, insurance and pensions Supply employment templates Assist recruitment and selection of Personal Assistants Operate a matching service where appropriate Assist with all aspects of pension auto-enrolment Promote safer employment by encouraging and facilitating the completion of enhanced DBS -Safeguarding and Compliance Promote safe recruitment Support DBS applications Attend safeguarding meetings when required Report and escalate risks to vulnerable adults, children and public funds. -Workforce Development Advise on training for Direct Payment users and Personal Assistants Promote professional development and competency frameworks -Other requirements Provide advice and practical assistance on request to social care professionals when needed Have a permanent base within Newcastle Expected usage: 487 adults are currently receiving a direct payment in Newcastle In the financial year 25/26 there were 315 people who used the service This notice is for information only. At this stage, no further details are available beyond what is published here. When this opportunity progresses, a Tender Notice will be published on the Central Digital Platform along with any relevant notices such as engagement.

records.title: Catering Services and Associated Goods
records.description: Reference: ACPHCS0001 Description: Perry Hall Multi-Academy Trust intends to procure a contract for the provision of catering services and associated goods across schools within the Trust. The procurement is intended to support the continued delivery of high-quality, safe, nutritious and value-for-money school meals whilst promoting pupil wellbeing, healthy eating, inclusion and sustainability. The Trust currently operates across a number of schools and is reviewing its future catering arrangements in advance of the expiry of its current catering contract in July 2027 Perry Hall Multi-Academy Trust currently comprises 10 primary schools serving approximately 3500 pupils total, across Wolverhampton and surrounding areas. The Trust reserves the right to include additional schools that may join the Multi-Academy Trust during the lifetime of the contract. The scope is expected to include: • Daily meal preparation and service. • Free School Meals (FSM), Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM) and paid meal provision. • Breakfast clubs, hospitality and special event catering. • Menu planning and nutritional compliance. • Food safety, allergen management and HACCP compliance. • Staffing, recruitment, training and workforce management. • Contract management, performance reporting and continuous improvement. • Sustainability initiatives, food waste reduction and responsible sourcing. • Engagement with pupils, parents, schools and Trust stakeholders. • Supply of associated catering consumables and ancillary goods where required. Suppliers will be expected to demonstrate: • Strong experience delivering school catering services within the education sector. • Robust safeguarding, food safety and allergen management arrangements. • Ability to improve meal uptake, customer satisfaction and nutritional outcomes. • Effective staffing resilience and mobilisation capability. • Strong reporting and contract management processes. • Commitment to social value, local employment opportunities and community benefits. • Environmental sustainability and responsible supply chain management. The Trust intends to use feedback received through its market engagement activity to help shape the final specification, performance framework, contract structure and evaluation methodology for the procurement. Particular emphasis will be placed on: • Food quality, nutritional standards and pupil experience. • Allergen management and statutory compliance. • Safeguarding and staff vetting requirements. • Service reliability and workforce resilience. • Contract performance management and continuous improvement. • Social value and sustainability outcomes. Perry Hall Multi-Academy Trust has appointed Altair Ltd to act as its official procurement agent for this tender. Altair Ltd will be managing market engagement responses, administrative queries, and tender communications on behalf of the Trust. All expressions of interest and engagement submissions should be directed to procurementaltair@altairltd.co.uk When the tender notice is published, the contracting authority will be using InTend as its eportal.

records.title: Passive Fire Safety Remedial works
records.description: The contract supports the delivery of passive fire protection works across our housing stock, including fire stopping, fire door repairs and replacements, glazing and fire compartmentation works. The service primarily relates to planned and remedial works arising from Fire Risk Assessments (FRAs) and fire door inspections, alongside a smaller volume of reactive works and specialist surveys. The re-procurement aims to deliver a more robust, compliant and efficient service that supports Southern Housing's fire safety strategy and long-term regulatory obligations. The proposed contract term is 5 years, with extension options of 2 + 2 + 1 years.
